snippet.title: Remembering XOXO 2019
snippet.description:
A look back at the seventh XOXO, held September 5-8, 2019 in Portland, Oregon— an experimental festival for independent artists who live and work online. Thanks to every attendee, speaker, artist, volunteer, and patron who made it so special. Find more information at https://xoxofest.com

Video by Searle Video. https://www.searlevideo.com/

Music: Left at London's "Revolution Lover"
Buy "Transgender Street Legend Vol. 1" on Bandcamp. https://leftatlondon.bandcamp.com/album/transgender-street-legend-vol-1

snippet.title: Rhea Butcher, Comic/Actor/Writer - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
Standup comic, actor, and writer Rhea Butcher co-created and starred in the critical hit TV series, Take My Wife, and their debut comedy album, Butcher, reached the top of the comedy charts. Rhea also hosts the popular live show and podcast, Put Your Hands Together, and their new podcast Three Swings takes an unconventional look at America's pastime.

Follow Rhea on Twitter: https://twitter.com/RheaButcher
Official Site: https://www.rheabutcher.com/
Upcoming Live Shows: https://www.rheabutcher.com/livedates/

—

Recorded in September 2019 at XOXO, an experimental festival in Portland, Oregon for independent artists and creators who work online. For more, visit https://xoxofest.com.

snippet.title: Nat Puff, Left At London - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
Left At London is the stage name of Nat Puff, a ferociously-talented indie pop artist and poet who built a cult following with her hilarious short videos on Vine. More recently, she produced a series breaking down how to make songs in the style of Mitski, Frank Ocean, and Tyler, the Creator. Her debut album, You Are Not Alone Enough, is due out later this year.

Nat opens her XOXO talk with a performance of "I Don't Trust U Anymore" off of Transgender Street Legend Vol. 1, and closes with a performance of "I Split My Ribs Open" with surprise special guest, Open Mike Eagle. Both songs can be found on Bandcamp here.
https://leftatlondon.bandcamp.com/album/transgender-street-legend-vol-1

Follow Left at London on Twitter: https://twitter.com/LeftAtLondon
Support her new webseries on Patreon: https://patreon.com/leftatlondon
Official Website: http://leftatlondon.com/

—

snippet.title: Lindsay Ellis, Video Essayist - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
With an MFA in film/TV production and the support of her dedicated Patreon base, Lindsay Ellis creates thoughtful and in-depth video essays about film criticism, pop culture, and a whole lot of Transformers. The day before XOXO 2019, Lindsay announced her debut novel, Axiom's End, will be published by St. Martin's Press next summer.

Watch Lindsay on YouTube: https://youtube.com/chezapoctube
Follow her on Twitter: https://twitter.com/thelindsayellis

snippet.description:

Combining social commentary with makeup tutorials, Jahkara built a following of over 445,000 subscribers in just over a year before switching it up to focus on her acting career.

snippet.description:
Chicago-based writer and cultural critic Mikki Kendall is the author of two upcoming books: Hood Feminism, a collection of essays on the blind spots of the modern feminist movement, and Amazons, Abolitionists, and Activists, a graphic history of the fight for women’s rights.

snippet.title: Jenny Odell, How to Do Nothing - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
In her first book, How to Do Nothing: Resisting the Attention Economy, multi-disciplinary artist and writer Jenny Odell argues that taking control of our attention from the capitalist forces determined to monetize it and reconnecting with the world around us is a critical form of resistance.

snippet.description:

Off-grid for long stretches, Hundred Rabbits is supported by patrons who follow along through video updates to their Patreon project.

snippet.title: Katherine Paul, Black Belt Eagle Scout - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
Black Belt Eagle Scout is the musical moniker of Katherine Paul, a radical indigenous queer feminist who grew up on a small reservation by the Salish Sea, the Swinomish Indian Tribal Community. Her sophomore album, At the Party With My Brown Friends, comes less than a year after her celebrated debut.

Official homepage: https://www.blackbelteaglescout.com/

snippet.title: Harry Brewis, Hbomberguy - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
Since 2014, Harry Brewis aka “Hbomberguy” built a base of over 450k YouTube subscribers with his wry video essays skewering the alt-right, Gamergate, and conspiracy theorists. In January, his Donkey Kong 64 charity stream went viral with cameos by AOC, Chelsea Manning and others, raising over $350,000 for Mermaids, a UK charity supporting gender-diverse and transgender children and young people.

snippet.title: Tracy Clayton, Another Round/Strong Black Legends - XOXO Festival (2019)
snippet.description:
Launched in 2015, Another Round quickly became one of the internet's most-loved podcasts, propelled by co-hosts Tracy Clayton and Heben Nigatu's candid banter about race, gender, and pop culture, taking a much-needed break at the end of 2017. After a year away from the mic, Tracy returned as host of Netflix’s Strong Black Legends, a weekly interview series with living legends of Black Hollywood.

Follow Tracy on Twitter: https://twitter.com/brokeymcpoverty

snippet.title: Cameron Esposito, Comedian/Actor/Podcaster - XOXO Festival (2018)
snippet.description:
Cameron Esposito pioneered inclusive television production with Take My Wife, her brilliant series with Rhea Butcher. Cameron’s new standup special, Rape Jokes, confronts issues of consent and sexual assault from a survivor’s perspective, raising over $93,000 for RAINN, the largest U.S. organization fighting sexual violence.

You can buy "Rape Jokes" on her website, with all proceeds going to RAINN, or watch it for free. https://www.cameronesposito.com/
